articles.title: Shortened Link Not Working or Redirection Failing
articles.problem: After shortening my URL from Dub, my link is not working, showing 404, or not redirecting to the destination.
articles.solution:
If your shortened URL is failing to redirect or showing an error, check these 4 common root causes:

### 1. Custom Domain DNS Inactive
If you shortened the link using a **custom domain** (e.g. `go.yourbrand.com`), its DNS records must be active:
• **Subdomain (e.g. go.brand.com):** CNAME pointing to `cname.dub.co`
• **Root Domain (e.g. brand.com):** A Record pointing to `76.76.21.21`
*(Tip: Type your domain below to run a live socket DNS diagnostic!)*

### 2. Broken Destination URL
Dub forwards visitors directly to your target destination URL. If your target URL is down, returning a `404 Not Found` or `500 Server Error`, the short link will appear broken. Test your target URL directly in an incognito window.

### 3. Link Status (Archived, Expired, or Click Limit)
In your Dub Dashboard under **Links**:
• Verify the link is toggled **Active** (not Archived).
• Check if an **Expiration Date** or **Click Limit** was previously configured.

### 4. SSL Certificate Provisioning Delay
If you recently connected your custom domain, Let's Encrypt automated SSL issuance takes **5 to 15 minutes** to propagate worldwide.

articles.title: UTM Parameters & Query String Forwarding
articles.problem: Are UTM tags and query parameters preserved when users click my short link?
articles.solution:
### Yes, Dub Automatically Forwards Query Parameters!

When a user clicks `yourbrand.com/sale?ref=twitter&utm_medium=social`, Dub automatically appends all incoming query parameters to the destination URL:

• **Original Destination:** `https://myshop.com/product`
• **Clicked Link:** `https://yourbrand.com/sale?utm_source=newsletter`
• **Final Redirect:** `https://myshop.com/product?utm_source=newsletter`

### Overriding Parameters:
If your short link already has built-in UTM parameters set in the Dub dashboard, incoming query parameters will cleanly merge without duplicating keys.

articles.title: Password-Protected Links
articles.problem: How do password-protected links work or why is my password not working?
articles.solution:
Dub allows you to gate any short link with a custom password.

### How It Works:
1. When a visitor clicks the link, Dub presents a branded, secure password prompt.
2. Upon entering the correct password, Dub securely sets an encrypted session cookie and redirects to the destination.

### Troubleshooting Password Issues:
• **Invalid Password:** Passwords are case-sensitive. Verify the exact string in your link settings.
• **Removing Password:** Go to Dub Dashboard ➔ Edit Link ➔ Clear the **Password** field ➔ Save.

articles.title: Expired Links & Click Limit Handling
articles.problem: What happens when a link expires or reaches its click limit?
articles.solution:
### Expired Link Behavior:
When a link reaches its `expiresAt` timestamp or exceeds its configured **Click Limit**:

1. **Custom Expired URL:** If configured, Dub redirects visitors to your custom fallback page (e.g. `https://yoursite.com/offer-ended`).
2. **Default Behavior:** If no fallback is configured, visitors see Dub's clean default 'Link Expired' landing page.

### How to Reactivate:
Go to your Dub Dashboard ➔ Click on the expired link ➔ Update or remove the **Expiration Date** or increase the **Click Limit**.

articles.title: Geo-Targeting & Device-Targeting (iOS / Android / Desktop)
articles.problem: How do I redirect iPhone users to App Store and Android users to Google Play?
articles.solution:
Dub supports dynamic edge-routing based on device and geolocation without latency penalties.

### Configuration Options:
• **iOS Redirect:** Set target URL for iPhone/iPad (e.g. `https://apps.apple.com/...`).
• **Android Redirect:** Set target URL for Android devices (e.g. `https://play.google.com/...`).
• **Geo-Location:** Route visitors by country code (e.g. US visitors to `.com`, UK visitors to `.co.uk`).
• **Default Fallback:** Catch-all destination for all other platforms and desktops.

articles.title: Custom Social Preview Cards (Open Graph / Twitter Cards)
articles.problem: My social preview image or title is not showing correctly when sharing on Twitter, Slack, or LinkedIn.
articles.solution:
Dub allows you to override default Open Graph (OG) metadata for any short link.

### How to Fix Social Preview Caching:
1. **Verify OG Image URL:** Ensure your preview image is publicly accessible, HTTPS, and ideally `1200x630px` (aspect ratio 1.91:1).
2. **Clear Social Media Cache:**
   • **Twitter/X:** Use Twitter Card Validator or paste link in a draft tweet.
   • **LinkedIn:** Use the [LinkedIn Post Inspector](https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/).
   • **Facebook:** Use the [Meta Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/).
3. **Custom Domain Benefit:** Using a custom branded domain ensures social networks display your brand instead of a generic domain.

articles.title: Short Link Flagged as Spam on LinkedIn, Twitter, or WhatsApp
articles.problem: My short link using dub.sh was blocked or flagged as malicious/spam on social media.
articles.solution:
### Root Cause:
Public shared domains like `dub.sh` or `bit.ly` occasionally get flagged by aggressive third-party spam heuristics when bad actors shorten suspicious URLs.

### The Permanent Solution: Use a Custom Branded Domain
1. Connect your own branded custom domain (e.g. `links.yourcompany.com` or `go.yourcompany.com`).
2. Branded domains carry your own domain reputation, 100% bypass third-party spam blocklists, and increase click-through rates by up to 39%.
3. Custom domains are included for free on Dub.

articles.title: Short Link Case Sensitivity & Lowercase Rewriting
articles.problem: Why does my short link fail with 404 when typed in lowercase, or how to enable case-insensitive links?
articles.solution:
### How Case Sensitivity Works in Dub

According to web standards (RFC 3986), URL paths and slugs are **case-sensitive** by default (`/MyLink` is technically distinct from `/mylink`).

### 1. Case-Insensitive Matching
In your Dub Dashboard under **Settings ➔ Domains**:
• Toggle **"Case-insensitive matching"** to ON.
• When enabled, incoming visits to `/SummerSale`, `/summersale`, and `/SUMMERSALE` will all seamlessly resolve to the same destination URL.

### 2. Automatic Lowercase Slugs
When creating links manually or via API:
• Best practice is to save slugs in lowercase (e.g., `brand.com/spring-sale`).
• If an uppercase slug is entered, Dub will automatically recommend lowercased aliases to prevent user 404 errors.

articles.title: Custom 404 Fallback & Root Domain Default Redirect
articles.problem: When visitors hit my root domain (go.brand.com/) or an invalid/non-existent short link, how do I redirect them to my homepage instead of showing 404?
articles.solution:
### Setting Default Redirect & 404 Fallback URLs

By default, visiting a custom domain's root (`https://go.yourbrand.com/`) or a typoed link returns a Dub 404 error page. You can customize this behavior:

### 1. Root Domain Default Redirect
1. Go to Dub Dashboard ➔ **Settings ➔ Domains**.
2. Click the three dots `...` next to your domain ➔ **Edit Domain**.
3. In the **Default Redirect URL** field, enter your main website:
   `https://yourcompany.com`
4. Now, any visitor navigating to `go.yourbrand.com` directly will land on your main website.

### 2. 404 Fallback Destination
In the same domain settings drawer:
• Set **404 Fallback URL** to a custom landing page or search page (e.g. `https://yourcompany.com/links`).
• Any mistyped, deleted, or expired slug will automatically forward visitors there rather than showing an error.

articles.title: Mobile Deep Linking, Universal Links & Custom App URI Schemes
articles.problem: How do I deep link directly into native iOS or Android mobile apps (e.g. spotify://, slack://, myapp://) with Dub?
articles.solution:
### Deep Linking Configuration in Dub

Dub supports routing mobile users directly into native mobile applications via **Custom URI Schemes** and **Universal Links / App Links**.

### How to Configure in Dashboard:
1. When creating or editing a link, open the **Targeting** drawer.
2. Under **Device Targeting**:
   • **iOS:** Enter your custom app scheme (e.g. `myapp://product/123`) or App Store link (`https://apps.apple.com/...`).
   • **Android:** Enter your Android intent or Google Play link (`https://play.google.com/...`).
   • **Default (Desktop/Web):** Enter the standard web destination (`https://mywebsite.com/product/123`).

### Deep Link Fallback Flow:
• Mobile user has app installed ➔ Phone opens the native app screen directly.
• Mobile user does not have app installed ➔ Dub redirects to App Store / Google Play fallback.
• Desktop user ➔ Opens the web version seamlessly.

articles.title: Configuring an Apex / Root Domain (e.g. yourdomain.com)
articles.problem: How do I configure my apex domain to work with Dub?
articles.solution:
Add an **A Record** in your DNS registrar (Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy):

| Type | Name / Host | Target IP | TTL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A** | `@` (or leave blank) | `76.76.21.21` | Auto / 3600 |

*Note: Dub automatically handles redirecting `www.yourdomain.com` to your root apex domain.*

articles.title: Configuring a Subdomain (e.g. go.yourdomain.com, links.yourdomain.com)
articles.problem: How do I configure a subdomain on Dub?
articles.solution:
Add a **CNAME Record** in your DNS provider:

| Type | Name / Host | Target Value | TTL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CNAME** | `go` or `links` | `cname.dub.co` | Auto / 3600 |

*Tip: Never enter the full domain in the Host field unless your DNS registrar explicitly requires it (e.g. enter 'go', not 'go.yourdomain.com').*

articles.title: Cloudflare DNS: Grey Cloud (DNS Only) vs Orange Cloud (Proxied)
articles.problem: My links are failing or throwing Error 525 / SSL handshake failed on Cloudflare.
articles.solution:
### Root Cause
Cloudflare's default proxy (**Orange Cloud**) intercepts traffic before Let's Encrypt certificates can complete verification with Dub's edge servers.

### How to Fix:
1. **Recommended (Instant Fix):** In your Cloudflare DNS tab, click the orange cloud toggle to switch it to **DNS Only (Grey Cloud)**.
2. **If Orange Cloud is mandatory:** Go to Cloudflare Dashboard ➔ **SSL/TLS** ➔ Change encryption mode to **Full** or **Full (Strict)**. *(Never use 'Flexible' mode)*.

articles.title: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS on Cloudflare
articles.problem: Domain gets stuck in an infinite redirect loop (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS).
articles.solution:
### Root Cause:
This happens when Cloudflare is set to **Flexible SSL**. Dub enforces HTTPS on port 443. Flexible SSL sends traffic to Dub over unencrypted HTTP (port 80), prompting Dub to redirect back to HTTPS, causing an infinite loop.

### Fix:
In your Cloudflare dashboard, go to **SSL/TLS** ➔ Change SSL/TLS encryption mode from **Flexible** to **Full** or **Full (Strict)**.

articles.title: SSL Certificate Pending / ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR
articles.problem: My domain says 'Invalid configuration' or browser shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR.
articles.solution:
1. SSL certificates are generated automatically via Let's Encrypt once your DNS records resolve.
2. Global DNS propagation typically takes **5 to 15 minutes**.
3. Make sure your domain points to `76.76.21.21` or `cname.dub.co`. Once resolved, click **Refresh** in your Dub domain dashboard.

articles.title: CAA Records Blocking SSL Issuance
articles.problem: SSL issuance fails because of Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) records.
articles.solution:
### Root Cause:
If your domain has CAA records in DNS, they restrict which Certificate Authorities can issue certificates for your domain.

### Fix:
Add a CAA record in your DNS provider permitting Let's Encrypt:

| Type | Name | Flag | Tag | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CAA** | `@` | `0` | `issue` | `letsencrypt.org` |

articles.title: Domain Previously Used on Vercel (Ownership Verification)
articles.problem: Dub error: 'Domain is already in use by another team/project on Vercel'.
articles.solution:
Because Dub operates on Vercel Anycast edge infrastructure, verify ownership by adding a TXT record:

| Type | Name / Host | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TXT** | `_vercel` | *(Copy token from Dub dashboard)* |

Once verified, the previous project mapping will be automatically released.

articles.title: GoDaddy DNS Configuration & Duplicate Subdomain Fix
articles.problem: How do I configure GoDaddy DNS for Dub and avoid the common duplicate subdomain bug?
articles.solution:
### GoDaddy DNS Setup Guide

Follow these exact steps in your GoDaddy DNS Manager:

### For Subdomain (e.g. `go.yourdomain.com`):
| Type | Name | Value | TTL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CNAME** | `go` *(DO NOT enter go.yourdomain.com)* | `cname.dub.co` | 1/2 Hour |

> ⚠️ **Common GoDaddy Trap:** GoDaddy automatically appends your root domain. If you enter `go.yourbrand.com` in the Name field, GoDaddy creates `go.yourbrand.com.yourbrand.com`, which will never resolve! Always enter just `go` or `links`.

### For Root / Apex Domain (e.g. `yourdomain.com`):
| Type | Name | Value | TTL |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A** | `@` | `76.76.21.21` | 1/2 Hour |

Delete any existing parked domain records or conflicting A records on `@` before saving.

articles.title: Namecheap Advanced DNS Configuration
articles.problem: How do I configure Namecheap DNS records for Dub and disable parking pages?
articles.solution:
### Namecheap DNS Setup Guide

1. Log in to Namecheap ➔ Go to **Domain List** ➔ Click **Manage** next to your domain.
2. Open the **Advanced DNS** tab.

### Required Records:
• **For Subdomain (`links.yourdomain.com`):**
  - Type: `CNAME Record`
  - Host: `links`
  - Target: `cname.dub.co.` *(include or omit trailing dot based on UI)*
  - TTL: `Automatic`

• **For Root Apex (`yourdomain.com`):**
  - Type: `A Record`
  - Host: `@`
  - Value: `76.76.21.21`
  - TTL: `Automatic`

### Troubleshooting Namecheap:
• Ensure **Namecheap Parking Page** record (URL Redirect / Parking) is deleted.
• If your nameservers are set to 'Namecheap Web Hosting DNS' or custom nameservers, Advanced DNS will not apply; switch nameservers to **Namecheap BasicDNS**.

articles.title: API Rate Limits & 429 Too Many Requests
articles.problem: I received HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when calling Dub API.
articles.solution:
### Rate Limit Thresholds (per minute):
• **Free Plan:** 60 requests/min
• **Pro Plan:** 600 requests/min
• **Business Plan:** 1,200 requests/min
• **Enterprise:** 3,000+ requests/min

### How to Resolve:
1. Check the `Retry-After` header to get the exact wait time in seconds.
2. Inspect `X-RateLimit-Remaining` to track your request quota.
3. For creating multiple links at once, use the **Bulk API** (`POST /links/bulk`) which processes up to 100 links per single request.

articles.title: Creating Links via REST API & SDK
articles.problem: How do I create a short link using Python or TypeScript?
articles.solution:
### 🚀 Create Short Link via REST API

**Endpoint:** `POST https://api.dub.co/links`  
**Headers:** `Authorization: Bearer <DUB_API_KEY>`

**Payload (JSON):**
```json
{
  "url": "https://yourcompany.com/blog/article",
  "domain": "go.yourdomain.com",
  "key": "spring-sale",
  "tags": ["marketing", "spring"],
  "trackConversion": true
}
```

**Python SDK Example:**
```python
from dub import Dub

client = Dub(token="DUB_API_KEY")
link = client.links.create(request={
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "domain": "go.mybrand.com"
})
print(link.short_link)
```

articles.title: Bulk Link Creation API (High Volume)
articles.problem: How do I create thousands of links without hitting rate limits?
articles.solution:
### Bulk Link Creation (`POST /links/bulk`)

Instead of making individual API calls, use the bulk endpoint to process up to **100 links per single request**:

**Endpoint:** `POST https://api.dub.co/links/bulk`

```json
[
  { "url": "https://acme.com/item1", "key": "item-1" },
  { "url": "https://acme.com/item2", "key": "item-2" }
]
```
*Note: Bulk creation counts as 1 request against your rate limit threshold!*

articles.title: HTTP 409 Conflict: Key Already Exists
articles.problem: API returns 409 Conflict when attempting to create a link.
articles.solution:
A link with that exact **slug / key** already exists for that domain.

### Options:
1. **Update existing link:** Use `PUT /links/{linkId}` or `PATCH /links/{linkId}`.
2. **Generate random slug:** Omit the `key` field in your payload and Dub will automatically assign a clean 7-character hash.

articles.title: HTTP 401 Unauthorized & 403 Forbidden
articles.problem: API calls returning 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.
articles.solution:
### 401 Unauthorized:
• Ensure header `Authorization: Bearer <DUB_API_KEY>` is included.
• Verify you did not accidentally copy extra whitespace or omit the `Bearer ` prefix.

### 403 Forbidden:
• Your API token does not have permission for the requested workspace.
• In Dub Dashboard ➔ Settings ➔ **API Keys**, ensure the key is assigned to the active workspace.

articles.title: Generating Dynamic QR Codes via API
articles.problem: How do I programmatically generate and customize QR codes for short links?
articles.solution:
### QR Code Endpoint

**Endpoint:** `GET https://api.dub.co/qr?url={url}`

### Query Parameters:
• `url` (required): Target short link URL.
• `logo`: URL of your brand logo to embed in the center.
• `size`: Image size in pixels (e.g. `600`).
• `level`: Error correction level (`L`, `M`, `Q`, `H`). Defaults to `H` when logo is present.
• `fgColor` / `bgColor`: Custom hex colors (e.g. `fgColor=%23000000`).

articles.title: Verifying Webhook HMAC SHA-256 Signatures
articles.problem: How do I securely verify that an incoming webhook payload was sent by Dub?
articles.solution:
Dub signs each payload with your signing secret in the `Dub-Signature` header.

### Python Verification Snippet:
```python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_signature(payload_bytes: bytes, signature_header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode("utf-8"), 
        payload_bytes, 
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature_header)
```

articles.title: Supported Webhook Events & Retry Policy
articles.problem: Which webhook events does Dub support and what happens if my receiver server is down?
articles.solution:
### Supported Events:
• `link.created` — Fired when a new short link is created.
• `link.updated` — Fired when link destination or settings change.
• `link.deleted` — Fired when a link is deleted.
• `link.clicked` — Real-time stream with country, city, device, browser, and referrer.

### Retry Policy:
If your server returns anything other than HTTP `2xx`, Dub retries delivery with exponential backoff for up to **3 days**.

articles.title: Metatags Scraping Edge Cases (Cloudflare, SPAs, TikTok, Instagram)
articles.problem: Why are metatags, title, and OpenGraph preview images not detected automatically or failing to scrape?
articles.solution:
### Why Automatic Metatag Scraping Can Fail

Dub automatically attempts to fetch OpenGraph and Twitter card metadata from your destination URLs. However, automatic scraping can fail under these conditions:

1. **Cloudflare Bot Management / Captcha:** If the target website blocks automated scrapers, Dub's bot receives a 403 Forbidden or captcha challenge.
2. **Client-Side SPAs (React/Vue/Vite without SSR):** If the page renders its `<meta>` tags purely through client-side JavaScript, the server-side scraper receives empty HTML.
3. **Walled Gardens (TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn):** These platforms strictly require authenticated session cookies to view content.

### The Solution: Explicit Manual Override
You do not need to rely on automatic scraping. You can specify exact metadata in the Dub dashboard or via the API:

```json
POST https://api.dub.co/links
{
  "url": "https://example.com/blocked-page",
  "title": "My Custom Viral Post",
  "description": "Exclusive sneak peek of our product launch.",
  "image": "https://assets.mybrand.com/banner.png"
}
```
Dub will cache and serve these custom metatags directly from its edge network, guaranteeing perfect social cards across Twitter, Slack, and iMessage!

articles.title: QR Code Scanning Issues & SVG Logo Customization
articles.problem: Why is my QR code unscannable on mobile cameras or why is the embedded logo missing/blurry in SVG downloads?
articles.solution:
### Ensuring 100% QR Code Scannability

If a QR code generated by Dub fails to scan on mobile devices, check these technical requirements:

### 1. Error Correction Level with Logos
When embedding a brand logo in the center of a QR code, the logo physically obscures 15% to 25% of the data grid.
• You **must** use Error Correction Level `H` (High - 30% recovery rate) when embedding logos.
• In the API, ensure `level=H` is passed: `GET https://api.dub.co/qr?url=...&logo=...&level=H`.

### 2. Foreground / Background Contrast Ratio
• QR code scanners require high optical contrast.
• Always use dark foreground colors (`fgColor=#000000` or `#1E293B`) on a pure white background (`bgColor=#FFFFFF`).
• Avoid yellow, pastel, or low-contrast colors on light backgrounds.

### 3. SVG vs PNG Logo Downloads
• When downloading as SVG, ensure your logo is a public, CORS-enabled HTTPS URL.
• If downloading for print billboards or high-dpi packaging, request high resolution: `size=1024`.

articles.title: Workspace Roles, Team Permissions & Scoped API Keys
articles.problem: How do workspace permissions work, and how can I create restricted API keys for developers or CI/CD pipelines?
articles.solution:
### Workspace Roles & Scoped API Keys

Dub provides granular role-based access control (RBAC) to keep workspace resources secure.

### Workspace Team Roles:
• **Owner:** Full administrative control. Can manage billing, invite/remove members, delete custom domains, and manage all links.
• **Member:** Can create, edit, archive, and view links and analytics. Cannot alter billing or workspace ownership.

### Scoped API Keys:
Never use an Owner token in frontend code, client applications, or third-party webhooks. Create restricted API keys in **Settings ➔ API Keys**:
• `links.write` — Create and update short links.
• `links.read` — Fetch link metadata and destinations.
• `analytics.read` — Query clickstream data and stats.
• `tags.write` — Manage campaign tags.

Restricted tokens prevent accidental workspace deletion or unauthorized domain remapping.

articles.title: Clicks Not Counting or Bot Filtering
articles.problem: Why do my link clicks look lower than external server logs or why are clicks filtered?
articles.solution:
### Intelligent Bot Filtering:
Dub automatically filters out automated scrapers, crawlers, and preview bots (e.g. Twitterbot, Slackbot, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp previews) to guarantee 100% human, accurate analytics.

### Inspecting Bot Clicks:
In your Dub Dashboard, toggle **Include Bot Traffic** in the analytics filter bar if you want to inspect raw crawler activity.

articles.title: Setting Up Conversion Tracking & Dub Analytics Pixel
articles.problem: How do I track signups and sales generated by short links?
articles.solution:
### Installing Dub Analytics Script

Add the script to your `<head>` tag:
```html
<script defer src="https://dub.co/tag.js" data-domain="yourdomain.com"></script>
```

### Tracking a Conversion Event (e.g. Signup or Purchase):
```javascript
window.dub?.track("Purchase", {
  amount: 49.00,
  currency: "USD"
});
```
Dub uses first-party cookies and privacy-first fingerprinting to tie conversions directly back to the original short link click.

articles.title: Exporting Click Data & Geographic Analytics to CSV
articles.problem: How can I export my analytics, raw click logs, and country/device breakdown to CSV format?
articles.solution:
### Exporting Analytics Data

Dub provides two ways to export your click and attribution data to CSV:

### 1. Direct Dashboard Export:
1. Navigate to the **Analytics** tab in your Dub Dashboard.
2. Select your desired date range (e.g. *Last 30 Days*, *Last 12 Months*, or *Custom Range*).
3. Click the **Export CSV** button in the top right corner.
4. The CSV will include total clicks, unique visitors, top countries, referrers, devices, and operating systems.

### 2. Programmatic Export via Analytics API:
Query the Dub REST API with the `export=csv` parameter:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.dub.co/analytics?event=clicks&groupBy=countries&export=csv" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DUB_API_KEY>"
```
You can also filter by specific `linkId`, `domain`, or `tagId` to isolate individual marketing campaign datasets.

articles.title: Stripe Checkout Webhook Integration & Revenue Attribution
articles.problem: How do I track actual revenue, Stripe checkout completions, and customer purchases generated by short links?
articles.solution:
### Connecting Short Links to Stripe Revenue

To attribute paying customers and MRR back to the exact link or influencer who referred them:

### Step 1: Capture the Dub Click Cookie
When a visitor arrives on your site via a Dub link, the `dub.co/tag.js` tracking script stores a unique click identifier in a first-party cookie named `dub_id`.

### Step 2: Pass `dub_id` into Stripe Checkout Session
When creating your Stripe Checkout session, include the `dub_id` in session metadata:
```python
session = stripe.checkout.Session.create(
    payment_method_types=['card'],
    line_items=[...],
    metadata={
        'dub_id': request.cookies.get('dub_id')
    }
)
```

### Step 3: Record the Conversion Event
In your Stripe webhook handler for `checkout.session.completed`:
```python
import requests

requests.post(
    "https://api.dub.co/track/customer",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {DUB_API_KEY}"},
    json={
        "customerId": event['data']['object']['customer'],
        "eventName": "Purchase",
        "amount": event['data']['object']['amount_total'] / 100,
        "currency": "USD"
    }
)
```
Dub will instantly attribute the sale to the initiating short link in your Analytics dashboard!

articles.title: Campaign Organization via Tags & Multi-Link Filtering
articles.problem: How do I organize thousands of short links by marketing campaign, client, or team using tags?
articles.solution:
### Organizing Links with Tags

Tags allow you to group, organize, and analyze links across multiple domains and teams.

### 1. Creating and Assigning Tags
• **Dashboard:** When creating or editing a link, type in the **Tags** field to select or create a tag (e.g. `black-friday-2026`, `youtube-influencers`, `changelog`).
• **API:** Pass an array of tag names or IDs:
  ```json
  POST https://api.dub.co/links
  {
    "url": "https://example.com/promo",
    "tags": ["black-friday", "newsletter"]
  }
  ```

### 2. Tag-Level Aggregated Analytics
In the Dub Analytics tab, filter by any tag to view aggregate metrics:
• Total clicks across all 50 links in a campaign.
• Global country and device distribution for that specific channel.
• Total conversions and revenue attributed to that tag.

articles.title: Self-Hosting Dub with Docker & Docker Compose
articles.problem: How do I self-host Dub on a VPS or Kubernetes cluster using Docker?
articles.solution:
### Self-Hosting Dub with Docker

Dub is 100% open-source under the AGPLv3 license. You can deploy it on your own server or VPS using Docker Compose.

### Minimum System Requirements:
• 2 CPU Cores, 4GB RAM
• Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+ recommended)
• Docker Engine 24.0+ and Docker Compose v2+

### Core Architecture Components:
1. **Frontend / API:** Next.js application container running on Node.js.
2. **Database:** PostgreSQL or MySQL database with Prisma schema migrations (`pnpm db:push`).
3. **Cache & Edge Key-Value:** Redis (Upstash Redis or local Redis instance).
4. **Click Analytics Engine:** Tinybird clickstream ingestion pipe (or ClickHouse for custom analytical pipelines).
5. **Storage:** Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3 for QR codes and OG image storage.

Run `git clone https://github.com/dubinc/dub.git`, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, configure the required variables, and run `docker compose up -d`.

articles.title: Self-Hosting Required Environment Variables & Services
articles.problem: What are the required environment variables and third-party services needed to self-host Dub?
articles.solution:
### Essential Environment Variables for Self-Hosting

When deploying Dub, configure the following keys in your `.env` file:

### 1. Database & Authentication:
• `DATABASE_URL`: Connection string for PostgreSQL or MySQL (e.g. `postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dub`).
• `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`: Random 32-character hex secret for session cookie encryption (`openssl rand -base64 32`).
• `NEXTAUTH_URL`: Your public domain (e.g. `https://dub.yourcompany.com`).

### 2. Redis & Rate Limiting:
• `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` & `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`: Required for edge caching, slug lookup speed, and rate-limiting.

### 3. Analytics & Background Jobs:
• `TINYBIRD_API_KEY`: Required for real-time click event ingestion and dashboard graphs.
• `QSTASH_TOKEN`: Upstash QStash for asynchronous webhook delivery and scheduled cron jobs.

### 4. Storage (QR Codes & Favicons):
• `STORAGE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` & `STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID`: Cloudflare R2 or S3 bucket credentials.

articles.title: Common Self-Hosting Errors & Build Failures
articles.problem: How do I fix common build errors (Prisma, Tinybird pipe errors, or Redis 403 Forbidden) when self-hosting?
articles.solution:
### Troubleshooting Common Self-Hosting Issues

### 1. Prisma Migration / Database Push Error:
• **Error:** `DatabaseError: Forbidden` or table mismatch.
• **Fix:** Run `pnpm db:push` to synchronize the Prisma schema with your database. Ensure your database user has `CREATE`, `ALTER`, and `INDEX` privileges.

### 2. Upstash Redis 403 Forbidden:
• Verify that `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` matches your Upstash REST API token (not standard Redis CLI password).
• Ensure your VPS IP is not firewalled by IP allowlists.

### 3. Tinybird Pipe Ingestion Errors:
• Make sure the Tinybird workspace was initialized using `tb auth` and the schema was pushed using `tb push`.
• Dub requires Tinybird pipes `dub_click_events_pipe` and `analytics_pipe` to populate analytics charts.

### 4. Next.js Turbo / Build Memory Limit:
• Running `pnpm build` in low-memory environments (under 2GB) can trigger `JavaScript heap out of memory`.
• Set `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=4096"` before running the build command.
